packages.label: מְפֻרְסָם וְיִסּוּרִין בִּשְׁבִיל רַבִּים
packages.label_en: The Famous One and Suffering on Behalf of the Many
packages.reason: Torah #71 teaches that public prominence (מְפֻרְסָם) carries an essential nature: the famous one becomes an aspect of Isaiah 53:12 — 'therefore I will divide him among the many' — and therefore must bear the quality of Isaiah 53:5 — 'by his stripes we are healed.' The famous tzaddik, the afflictions he suffers, the masses he heals, and the verse-formula of the Suffering Servant are all parallel expressions of one essential reality: public holiness requires absorbing the pain of others. The Rebbe says explicitly 'הוּא בִּבְחִינוֹת: לָכֵן אֲחַלֶּק לוֹ בָרַבִּים' — the famous person IS in the aspect of this verse, and 'עָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: וּבַחֲבֻרָתוֹ נִרְפָּא לָנוּ' — of him it is said, by his wounds we are healed. These are bechina-declarations (בְּחִינוֹת / נֶאֱמַר) linking the concept of public prominence to the entire Isaiah-53 theology of redemptive suffering. Paragraph 2 extends this to tzaddikim who voluntarily accept suffering to exchange the divine flow (שֶׁפַע), which is the same essential nature seen from a different angle: the tzaddik who absorbs communal suffering and thereby transforms the quality of the divine outpouring. All concepts belong to one unified domain — the structural reality of the tzaddik who bears the suffering of the many.
packages.note_on_degrees: Degrees are inferred from source-text bechina structure, not from torahData.js edges (which are absent for reference===71). מְפֻרְסָם holds the highest degree because it is the subject of both the בְּחִינוֹת declaration (linked to Isaiah 53:12) and the נֶאֱמַר formula (linked to Isaiah 53:5). יִסּוּרִין בִּשְׁבִיל רַבִּים bridges Paragraphs 1 and 2 — it is mentioned in both as the mechanism connecting the public tzaddik to the healing of the many, and as the voluntary act of the tzaddikim in Paragraph 2.
